description.value: A creature that touches the dragon or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet takes 7 (2d6) fire damage.
If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Immune to fire damage. Resistant to thunder. Vulnerable to cold (takes additional damage).
The dragon makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.
The dragon exhales fire in a 60-ft cone. Each creature in the area makes a DC 18 Dexterity save, taking 56 (16d6) fire damage on a failed save, or half on a successful one.

The dragon roars with enough force that the air itself cracks. Each creature within 30 ft makes a DC 18 Constitution save, taking 36 (8d8) thunder damage and being deafened for 1 minute on a failure, or half damage and no deafening on a success.
The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The dragon makes a tail lash attack.
The dragon spits a single ember at a point within 60 ft. Each creature within 5 ft of that point makes a DC 18 Dexterity save, taking 14 (4d6) fire damage on a failure or half on a success.

biography.value:
An adult of the Crimson Brood — long-bodied, serpentine, with stub wings used more for balance and intimidation than sustained flight. Twenty feet from snout to tail and burning hot enough to set dry wood smoldering at ten paces. Eyes that emit ember-orange light into pitch darkness.

Tactics

Akakkō adults open with intimidation and demands; if those fail, they prefer melee — claws, jaws, and the heat of their own bodies. They will use Cinderbreath against grouped enemies but waste it disdainfully against single targets unless cornered. They fight to the death when challenged on hospitality grounds; they retreat readily if the fight has become merely tactical.

Lair Actions

On initiative count 20 (losing ties), the dragon takes a lair action. The dragon cannot use the same lair action two rounds in a row.

  • Magma Surge. A 10-ft-radius column of molten rock erupts from the floor at a point the dragon can see within 120 ft. Each creature in the column makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 18 (4d8) fire damage on a failure or half on a success. The space becomes difficult terrain (cooling magma) until the start of the dragon's next turn.
  • Heat Distortion. The air within 60 ft of the dragon shimmers; ranged weapon attack rolls against the dragon are made at disadvantage until initiative count 20 of the next round.
  • Volcanic Tremor. Each creature on the ground within the lair makes a DC 14 Strength save or falls prone.

Regional Effects

The region within 6 miles of an Akakkō lair shows the dragon's influence:

  • The air is uncomfortably warm; ambient temperature runs 10°F above natural baseline.
  • Open flames burn brighter and consume fuel half as fast.
  • Once per day, a creature that finishes a long rest within 1 mile of the lair must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or gain no benefit from the rest, troubled by ember-dreams.

If the dragon is killed or driven away, these effects fade over the following 1d10 days.

description.value: A creature that touches the wyrmling or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet takes 3 (1d6) fire damage.
The wyrmling exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 (5d8) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

biography.value:
A young Crimson Brood dragon, no larger than a wolf but already burning with the volcanic temperament of its parent line. Glossy black scales rim along the back with red-orange ridges that glow brighter when the wyrmling is excited or angered. Its breath smells of struck flint.

Behavior

Bold, easily provoked, easily impressed. Akakkō wyrmlings will challenge anything they think they can defeat — and they think they can defeat almost anything. They respect demonstrations of strength and despise hesitation.

As a Bonded Companion

When granted as a Wyrmling Bond (Tomo-no-Chigiri), use the Warrior sidekick template (Tasha's). The wyrmling levels with its bonded PC, gaining sidekick class features in addition to the base stat block.

description.value: The dragon can breathe air and water.
If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Immune to cold and lightning. Vulnerable to fire (takes additional damage).
The dragon makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

The dragon exhales a 60-ft line of cold sea and lightning, 5 ft wide. Each creature in the line makes a DC 18 Dexterity save, taking 33 (6d10) cold damage and 22 (4d10) lightning damage on a failure, or half on a success.
When the dragon is hit by an attack while in or adjacent to a body of water at least 5 ft deep, it may reduce the damage by 4d8.
The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The dragon makes a tail lash attack.
The dragon glimpses a moment in the immediate future. The next attack roll made against it before the start of its next turn is made at disadvantage.

biography.value:
An adult of the Azure Brood — twenty-five feet of eel-bodied serpent with broad sail-fins running from head to tail, capable of swimming faster than any sailing vessel and gliding above the waves on storm-winds. Long whiskers like a carp; eyes like banked lightning.

Tactics

Aokkō adults prefer to engage from range, calling lightning from above while submerged out of reach. They use the Sea-Reading reaction to redirect attacks into water, where they take half damage. They retreat into deep water when bloodied and rarely fight to the death — long memory makes them patient.

Lair Actions

On initiative count 20 (losing ties), the dragon takes a lair action.

  • Drowning Surge. A 20-ft cube of seawater erupts at a point within 120 ft. Each creature in the cube makes a DC 15 Strength save or is restrained and unable to breathe air until the start of the dragon's next turn.
  • Storm-Call. Lightning strikes a point within 120 ft. Each creature within 5 ft makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) lightning damage on a failure or half on a success.
  • Tide Pull. Each creature within 60 ft of the dragon must make a DC 14 Strength save or be pulled 20 ft toward the dragon.

Regional Effects

Within 6 miles of an Aokkō lair:

  • Fog rolls in unbidden during the dragon's waking hours, regardless of weather.
  • Tides run an hour off the lunar pattern.
  • Drowning creatures within 1 mile die slower than they should — a small mercy or a deliberate cruelty, depending on the dragon's mood.

description.value: The dragon can breathe air and water.
Immune to cold and lightning. Vulnerable to fire.

The wyrmling exhales a line of churning sea-storm 30 ft long and 5 ft wide. Each creature in the line makes a DC 12 Dexterity save, taking 13 (3d8) cold damage and 9 (2d8) lightning damage on a failed save, or half on a successful one.

biography.value:
A young Azure Brood dragon — eel-like, sail-finned, the length of a tall man head to tail. Scales the color of dawn over a calm sea, fading to mother-of-pearl on the belly. The wyrmling drips constantly when out of water, leaving small puddles that smell of salt.

Behavior

Watchful, distant, slow to acknowledge a stranger. Aokkō wyrmlings observe long before they engage, and they remember every kindness and every cruelty.

As a Bonded Companion

When granted as a Wyrmling Bond, use the Expert sidekick template (Tasha's). Aokkō companions excel at scouting, perception, and oceanic navigation.

description.value: The borei casts Counterspell or Shield as a reaction.
The borei makes three Divine Burst attacks.
The borei casts Counterspell (3rd level, Intelligence-based, DC 13).
The borei casts Shield, gaining +5 AC until the start of its next turn.
The borei casts Misty Step (2/day).

biography.value:
A bōrei is a powerful seimaster — a mage of significant skill who channels sei through intellect and study. They command devastating evocation magic including Fireball and Cone of Cold, protect themselves with Shield and Counterspell, and can teleport short distances with Misty Step. A bōrei in its element is among the most dangerous opponents an adventuring party can face.

Tactics

Bōrei fight methodically: Mage Armor before combat, Misty Step to maintain distance, Fireball or Cone of Cold against groups, and Divine Burst for sustained single-target damage. They use Counterspell and Shield reactively to survive focused attacks.

Spells

Detect Magic, Light, Mage Armor, Mage Hand, Prestidigitation, Fireball, Invisibility, Cone of Cold, Fly, Spirit Guardians, Misty Step, Counterspell, Shield

Nature

undefined

The term 'bōrei' literally means 'departed spirit' but in common usage refers to any powerful seimaster who has devoted their life to magical study. Not all bōrei are hostile — some are reclusive scholars, court advisors, or wandering sages. The stat block represents a combat-ready mage of considerable power.

description.value: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Immune to cold. Resistant to radiant. Vulnerable to fire (takes additional damage).
The dragon casts no shadow under any natural or magical light.
The dragon knows when any creature within 1 mile is acting in a way it has never acted before.
The dragon makes three attacks: one bite and two claws.

The dragon exhales a 60-ft cone of bitter starlight. Each creature in the area makes a DC 18 Constitution save, taking 36 (8d8) cold damage and 27 (6d8) radiant damage on a failure, or half on a success.

When the dragon is hit by an attack, it may teleport up to 30 ft to a moonlit or starlit space, taking the damage in its new position. If the attack was ranged, the attacker must reroll against the dragon's new AC.
The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The dragon makes a tail lash attack.

The dragon designates one creature within 120 ft. Until the start of the dragon's next turn, attacks against the marked creature are made at advantage and the marked creature glows with cold starlight, granting no benefit from being invisible.

biography.value:
An adult of the Silver Brood — thirty feet long, slender, double-winged. Liquid silver scales reflect constellations that do not match the sky overhead; sometimes the reflection is the sky as it was a thousand years ago, sometimes the sky as it will be a thousand years hence. Eyes like the seas of the moon.

Tactics

Ginkkō adults rarely engage on their own initiative. When they do, they treat the encounter as a study; they will retreat to consider any combatant who proves interesting and return on their own schedule. They prefer cold and freezing tactics to outright kills, and they teleport between moonlit and starlit spaces to keep distance.

Lair Actions

On initiative count 20 (losing ties):

  • Constellation Step. The dragon teleports up to 120 ft to any moonlit or starlit space it can see. If a creature attacks the dragon during this round, the dragon's space at the start of its turn is illusory; the attack resolves against the empty space.
  • Sky-Pull. The dragon designates a 20-ft cube within 120 ft. Each creature in the cube makes a DC 16 Strength save or is pulled 30 ft toward the dragon and restrained until the start of the dragon's next turn (frozen midair in cold light).
  • Moonshard. A shard of crystallized moonlight strikes a point within 120 ft. Each creature within 10 ft makes a DC 16 Dexterity save, taking 22 (4d10) cold damage on a failure or half on a success.

Regional Effects

Within 6 miles of a Ginkkō lair:

  • Nights are clearer and stars brighter than the latitude should allow.
  • Compasses point to the lair rather than to magnetic north.
  • Time passes a fraction more slowly than elsewhere; a long rest within 1 mile lasts 9 hours of subjective time but ends at the same dawn as the rest of the world.

description.value: Immune to cold. Resistant to radiant. Vulnerable to fire.
The wyrmling casts no shadow under any natural or magical light.

The wyrmling exhales a 15-ft cone of bitter starlight. Each creature in the area makes a DC 12 Constitution save, taking 13 (3d8) cold damage and 9 (2d8) radiant damage on a failed save, or half on a successful one.

biography.value:
A young Silver Brood dragon — slender, long-tailed, with a second smaller pair of wings trailing like ribbons. Scales liquid silver that already shows pinpoint reflections of constellations no longer visible from the present sky. Eyes the color of the moon's seas. The wyrmling leaves no footprints on snow.

Behavior

Distant. Contemplative. Genuinely uninterested in mortal politics. Ginkkō wyrmlings observe far more than they engage and tend to speak only when asked direct questions.

As a Bonded Companion

When granted as a Wyrmling Bond, use the Spellcaster sidekick template (Tasha's). Ginkkō companions favor divinatory and cold magic. They speak rarely and never about themselves.

description.value: While in sunlight, the kageban has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
The kageban does not require air, food, drink, or sleep.
The kageban makes two Life Drain or Grave Bolt attacks.

The target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

biography.value:
A Kageban — Shadow Sentinel — is a restless undead bound to serve as a guardian or spy. Unlike mindless undead, kageban retain cunning intelligence and can employ magic to deceive and destroy. They appear as gaunt, shadowy humanoid figures with hollow eyes that glow with dim spectral light.

Behavior

Kageban are tactical combatants that use Disguise Self to infiltrate, Fear to scatter groups, and their Life Drain to weaken isolated targets. They often serve more powerful undead or necromancers as lieutenants.

Creation

undefined

A kageban is created when a warlock or sorcerer dies while bound by a pact to an entity of shadow or death. The pact energy sustains the corpse beyond death, creating an intelligent undead that retains fragments of its magical ability.

description.value: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Immune to radiant. Resistant to force. Vulnerable to necrotic (takes additional damage).
The dragon has advantage on saves vs. illusions, cannot be charmed, and cannot be deceived by mundane lies — it knows when a creature is speaking falsely.
Each enemy that starts its turn within 10 ft of the dragon takes 11 (2d10) radiant damage.
The dragon makes three attacks: one bite and two claws.

The dragon exhales brilliant gold light in a 60-ft cone. Each creature in the area makes a DC 21 Constitution save, taking 71 (13d10) radiant damage on a failure or half on a success. Undead and aberrations have disadvantage on this save.
When an ally within 30 ft is hit by an attack the dragon judges to be unjust, the dragon may negate the attack — the effect simply does not occur. Once per round.
The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The dragon makes a tail lash attack.
The dragon speaks a single word. One creature within 60 ft makes a DC 21 Wisdom save or is incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

Brilliant gold light flashes around the dragon. Each enemy within 30 ft makes a DC 21 Constitution save, taking 27 (6d8) radiant damage and being blinded until the end of its next turn on a failure, or half damage and no blinding on a success.

biography.value:
An adult of the Golden Brood — thirty-five feet of magnificent dragon, mane-crested with fine gold filament that catches every breeze. Scales the warm gold of dawn light. Breath that smells of incense and clean rain. The dragon does not radiate power so much as inhabit it; standing in its presence feels like standing in a courtroom that has somehow extended to the horizon.

Tactics

Kinkkō adults do not strike first. They will speak, sometimes at length, before initiative is rolled — and the conversation is not stalling but evaluation. When they fight, they fight precisely and lethally, but they accept surrender at any point and will protect allies who have surrendered. They do not retreat. They do not need to.

Lair Actions

On initiative count 20 (losing ties):

  • Pillar of Light. A pillar of brilliant gold light, 10 ft radius and 60 ft tall, descends at a point within 120 ft. Each creature in the pillar makes a DC 18 Constitution save, taking 33 (6d10) radiant damage on a failure or half on a success. Undead and aberrations have disadvantage.
  • Sovereign Word. The dragon speaks a word of authority. Each hostile creature within 60 ft makes a DC 18 Wisdom save or is restrained until the start of the dragon's next turn.
  • Reflect Injustice. The next time a hostile creature within 60 ft makes an attack against an ally of the dragon (including a petitioner the dragon has accepted), the attacker takes 22 (4d10) radiant damage.

Regional Effects

Within 6 miles of a Kinkkō lair:

  • Sunlight is brighter and reaches further; deception magic of 5th level or lower fails within 1 mile.
  • Sleeping within sight of the lair grants prophetic dreams to any creature with a true intention to act justly.
  • Honest creatures know the way to the lair without map or guide; dishonest creatures find themselves walking in circles.

description.value: Immune to radiant damage. Resistant to force. Vulnerable to necrotic.
The wyrmling has advantage on saves vs. illusions and cannot be charmed.

The wyrmling exhales a 20-ft cone of golden light. Each creature in the area makes a DC 13 Constitution save, taking 27 (6d8) radiant damage on a failed save, or half on a successful one. Undead and aberrations have disadvantage on this save.

biography.value:
A young Golden Brood dragon — already classically draconic in shape, four legs, broad wings, a sweeping tail. The wyrmling's scales are warm gold, the color of dawn light rather than coin-metal. Eyes the color of polished amber. Even at this age, the wyrmling carries itself with deliberate dignity.

Behavior

Just, careful, slow to commit. Kinkkō wyrmlings refuse instructions they consider dishonorable and are not impressed by displays of power that lack purpose. They will leave a bonded PC who orders the murder of a non-combatant.

As a Bonded Companion

When granted as a Wyrmling Bond, use the Warrior sidekick template (Tasha's). Kinkkō wyrmlings are observably brighter than ordinary creatures and cannot be hidden indefinitely.

description.value: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Immune to necrotic. Resistant to psychic. Vulnerable to radiant (takes additional damage).
While in dim light or darkness, the dragon can take the Hide action as a bonus action even while observed.
The dragon knows the location of every creature within 1 mile that is currently keeping a secret it considers significant.
The dragon makes three attacks: one bite and two claws.

The dragon exhales a 60-ft cone of corrosive whispers. Each creature in the area makes a DC 19 Wisdom save, taking 49 (11d8) psychic damage on a failure or half on a success. On a failure, the creature is also stunned until the end of its next turn.
When a creature within 60 ft makes a saving throw against being charmed, frightened, or against an illusion, the dragon may impose disadvantage on the save.
The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The dragon makes a tail lash attack.
One creature within 120 ft makes a DC 19 Wisdom save or has disadvantage on its next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw made before the start of the dragon's next turn.

biography.value:
An adult of the Onyx Brood — thirty feet of segmented, centipede-like dragon with two great wings folded close. Eyeless. Voiceless in the air. Yet the air around the dragon hums with whispers in twenty different languages, all of them just below the threshold of comprehension.

Tactics

Kurokkō adults rarely fight in the open. They negotiate first, and their negotiations are sincere — but they have read every hesitation and every secret in the petitioner's mind before the petitioner finishes speaking. If combat is forced, they fight to disable rather than kill, preferring captives to corpses. Captives can pay debts.

Lair Actions

On initiative count 20 (losing ties):

  • Whisper-Web. Each creature within the lair must make a DC 16 Wisdom save or have its mind brushed by the dragon's awareness; on a failure, the dragon learns one true thing about the creature it did not previously know.
  • Shadow Lance. A line of cold darkness 60 ft long, 5 ft wide stabs from a point the dragon can see. Each creature in the line makes a DC 16 Dexterity save, taking 27 (6d8) necrotic damage on a failure or half on a success.
  • Step Through Shadow. The dragon teleports up to 60 ft to any unoccupied space in dim light or darkness.

Regional Effects

Within 6 miles of a Kurokkō lair:

  • Secrets weigh heavier. Creatures attempting to deceive others have disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.
  • Lights gutter unpredictably; torches and candles burn at half their normal duration.
  • The dragon learns the name and one true memory of any creature that sleeps within 1 mile.

description.value: Immune to necrotic damage. Resistant to psychic. Vulnerable to radiant.
While in dim light or darkness, the wyrmling can take the Hide action as a bonus action.

The wyrmling exhales a 15-ft cone of corrosive whispers. Each creature in the area makes a DC 12 Wisdom save, taking 22 (5d8) psychic damage on a failed save, or half on a successful one. On a failure, the creature also drops one item of the wyrmling's choice.

biography.value:
A young Onyx Brood dragon — long, segmented, multiple short pairs of legs. Scales drink light. The wyrmling has no visible eyes; it perceives by heat, sei, and a subtler sense it does not explain. Its voice arrives in the listener's skull rather than through the air.

Behavior

Quiet. Watchful. Transactional. Kurokkō wyrmlings deal in promises and small secrets even before they can speak in formal sentences. They are pleasant company in a way that is faintly unsettling.

As a Bonded Companion

When granted as a Wyrmling Bond, use the Expert sidekick template (Tasha's). The wyrmling extracts one secret per week from the bonded PC; track the count in Obsidian/dm/campaign-state.md.

description.value: If the dragon fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
Immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition. Vulnerable to fire.
The dragon can communicate with plants at will as the spell.
The dragon makes three attacks: one bite, one antler-gore, and one tail lash.

The dragon exhales rotting spores in a 60-ft cone. Each creature in the area makes a DC 18 Constitution save, taking 56 (16d6) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. Plant creatures and undead are unaffected.
The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.
The dragon makes an antler-gore attack.
The dragon or one ally within 60 ft regains 14 (4d6) hit points.

biography.value:
An adult of the Emerald Brood — twenty feet of stocky, four-legged dragon with a magnificent antler crown that branches like ancient oak. Moss and lichen grow visibly along the back; small mushrooms sprout in the joints between scales. The dragon trails wildflowers in its footprints.

Tactics

Midokkō adults are reluctant combatants. They use entangling magic and Spore Cloud to hold attackers at bay, healing themselves and allies between rounds. They prefer to drive intruders away rather than kill them — but they will kill those who burn living things, and those they kill they do not mourn.

Lair Actions

On initiative count 20 (losing ties):

  • Verdant Snare. Roots and vines erupt in a 20-ft cube within 120 ft. Each creature in the cube makes a DC 15 Strength save or is restrained until the start of the dragon's next turn.
  • Renewing Bloom. The dragon and one ally within 60 ft regain 22 (4d10) hit points.
  • Mushroom Spore Burst. A 10-ft-radius sphere of poisonous spores blooms at a point within 120 ft. Each creature in the area makes a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 18 (4d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success.

Regional Effects

Within 3 miles of a Midokkō lair:

  • Plants grow at twice their natural rate.
  • Injured beasts within 1 mile heal twice as fast.
  • Felling a living tree within 1 mile alerts the dragon as surely as a struck bell.

description.value: Immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition. Vulnerable to fire.
The wyrmling can communicate with plants as if under the effect of speak with plants at will.
The wyrmling exhales a 15-ft cone of rotting spores. Each creature in the area makes a DC 12 Constitution save, taking 22 (5d8) poison damage on a failed save, or half on a successful one.

biography.value:
A young Emerald Brood dragon — stocky, four-legged, antlers just sprouting like a yearling stag's. Scales already overgrowing with moss along the back. Eyes deep amber and slit-pupiled like a goat's. The wyrmling smells faintly of forest floor and warm rain.

Behavior

Patient beyond its years. Midokkō wyrmlings rarely act in haste; they prefer to observe, to tend small living things, to wait. When pressed, they fight defensively rather than aggressively.

As a Bonded Companion

When granted as a Wyrmling Bond, use the Spellcaster sidekick template (Tasha's). Midokkō companions favor druidic and healing magic and refuse to enter cities for more than a day at a time.

description.value: If the ashigaru takes any damage from an attack or as the result of a failed saving throw, its hit points are reduced to 0. If the ashigaru takes damage that fails to kill it from other effects, it takes no damage instead.
The ashigaru has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the ashigaru's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

biography.value:
The lowest rank of nagaji warrior, ashigaru are expendable foot soldiers bred in great numbers. They fight with simple spears and shortbows, relying on overwhelming numbers rather than individual skill. Their serpentine features are less pronounced than higher-caste nagaji — flatter faces, duller scales, smaller builds.

Tactics

Ashigaru fight as minions — individually fragile but dangerous in groups. A single blow fells one, but a dozen more fill the gap. They are disciplined enough to hold formation and follow orders from higher-ranked nagaji.

Hierarchy

undefined

Ashigaru are the product of selective breeding by nagaji priesthoods, optimized for obedience and numbers over individual strength. They occupy the lowest rung of nagaji society, serving as expendable labor and cannon fodder.

description.value: The bushi has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
The bushi has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects that deal acid or poison damage.
The bushi makes two Katana attacks or two Daikyu attacks.

Recharge 5-6. The bushi channels sei into a devastating overhead katana strike. One creature within 5 feet must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d10 + 4 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. On a failed save, the target is also knocked prone.
The bushi adds 2 to its AC against one melee attack that would hit it. To do so, the bushi must see the attacker and be wielding a melee weapon.

biography.value:
Nagaji bushi are elite warriors clad in enchanted chain mail, wielding katanas and longbows with lethal precision. Their scales are thick and iridescent, a mark of superior breeding. Bushi serve as champions, bodyguards to priests, and commanders of lesser nagaji forces.

Tactics

Bushi are straightforward but devastating combatants — high AC from magical armor, strong multiattack with katanas, and longbow capability at range. They anchor nagaji battle lines and are often the most dangerous individual opponent in a nagaji warband.

Status

undefined

Bushi hold honored positions in nagaji society, second only to the priestly caste. They are bred for strength and resilience, and many bear ritual scarification marking their kills and achievements.

description.value: The hohei has advantage on saving throws against being frightened.
The hohei makes two Yari attacks.

biography.value:
Nagaji hohei — infantry — are a step above ashigaru, equipped with better armor and trained to fight in coordinated pairs. Their scales show more vivid coloring, marking them as a higher breed. They wield spears and shortbows with disciplined precision.

Tactics

Hohei fight with multiattack capability, striking twice per round. They form the backbone of nagaji warbands, providing reliable melee and ranged pressure while ashigaru absorb initial casualties.

Role

undefined

Hohei serve as the standard garrison force of nagaji strongholds. Where ashigaru are expendable, hohei are trusted with guard duty, patrol routes, and holding key positions during battle.

description.value: Magical darkness doesn't impede the kannushi's darkvision.
When the kannushi casts a spell that deals damage, it can change the damage type to necrotic.
The kannushi makes two Shinsei no Dageki attacks.

biography.value:
Nagaji kannushi are high priests of the serpent deity, commanding powerful divine magic alongside martial skill. They see through magical darkness with Devil's Sight, resist necrotic energy, and wield devastating spells including Cone of Cold and Spirit Guardians. A kannushi typically leads a nagaji force of dozens.

Tactics

Kannushi open with area spells — Spirit Guardians for sustained damage, Fear to break morale, Cone of Cold for burst damage. They use Hold Person to neutralize dangerous threats and Shield of Faith on their bushi bodyguards. In melee they are competent but prefer to direct from behind the front line.

Spells

Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy, Command, Inflict Wounds, Shield of Faith, Hold Person, Spiritual Weapon, Spirit Guardians, Fear, Cone of Cold

Role

undefined

Kannushi interpret the will of the serpent deity and direct nagaji communities. They are both spiritual leaders and military commanders, wielding authority through divine mandate and raw magical power.

description.value: The sohei's movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
The sohei makes two attacks: one with its Yari and one Unarmed Strike, or two Unarmed Strikes.

biography.value:
Nagaji sōhei are warrior-monks who blend martial prowess with limited divine magic granted by their serpent deity. They fight with unarmed strikes and spears, their movements unnaturally fluid. Sōhei serve as enforcers, squad leaders, and temple guardians.

Tactics

Sōhei combine melee multiattack with support spells — Command to disrupt enemies and Shield of Faith to bolster allies. They are faster than standard humanoids, moving with serpentine grace.

Spells

Sacred Flame, Thaumaturgy, Command, Shield of Faith

Role

undefined

Sōhei undergo rigorous training in nagaji monasteries, learning to channel divine sei through martial forms. They answer to kannushi priests and serve as the bridge between the warrior and priestly castes.

description.value: The zasu has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
Magical darkness doesn't impede the zasu's darkvision.
The zasu makes three Bite attacks, or it uses Spectral Fangs twice.
If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 poison damage.
A spectral serpent head strikes at a creature within range.

The zasu channels the torpor of its patron. Each creature of the zasu's choice within 30 feet must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or fall unconscious for 1 minute. A sleeping target awakens if it takes damage or if another creature uses an action to wake it. Undead and creatures immune to being charmed are unaffected.

biography.value:
The nagaji zasu — high priest — is a monstrous serpentine being that has transcended its humanoid origins through dark pact magic. Unlike the divine kannushi, the zasu draws power from a patron entity, granting it Magic Resistance, Devil's Sight, and the ability to put entire groups to sleep with Merrshaulk's Slumber.

Tactics

The zasu opens with Merrshaulk's Slumber to incapacitate multiple targets, then uses Spectral Fangs at range or closes for a devastating triple Bite attack that delivers piercing and poison damage. It uses Suggestion and Hold Person to control dangerous opponents.

Spells

Animal Friendship (snakes only), Guidance, Mage Hand, Message, Suggestion, Hold Person, Invisibility

Nature

undefined

A zasu is classified as a monstrosity rather than a humanoid — its pact magic has physically transformed it, granting darkvision out to 120 feet and immunity to poison. It has more in common with a yuan-ti abomination than a humanoid priest.

Merrshaulk

undefined

The name 'Merrshaulk's Slumber' references an entity of serpentine power. Whether this is the same being as the yuan-ti god or a distinct Kagekuni entity remains unclear.

description.value: The swarm has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in dim light or darkness.
The swarm can occupy another creature's space and vice versa, and the swarm can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny rat. The swarm can't regain hit points or gain temporary hit points.
The swarm has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

The swarm deals 2d6 piercing damage, or 1d6 piercing damage if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer. A creature that takes damage must succeed on a DC 9 Constitution saving throw or take 1 necrotic damage as shadow-tainted saliva seeps into the wounds.

biography.value:
A churning mass of tiny dark-furred rats with glinting red eyes. Yaminezumi swarms gather in sewers, abandoned buildings, and forest undergrowth, drawn together by some instinct darker than mere hunger. They flow like a living tide, climbing walls and pouring through gaps barely wider than a finger.

Behavior

Yaminezumi swarms are aggressive when disturbed and will pursue prey relentlessly through narrow spaces. They scatter only when reduced to a handful of survivors.

Ecology

undefined

Yaminezumi are touched by shadow — their eyes glow faintly in darkness, and they seem to thrive in places where the boundary between the material and spirit world is thin. Some scholars believe they are attracted to sites of death or dark sei.

description.value: The onryo can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 1d10 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
While in sunlight, the onryo has disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

The target must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or its hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hit point maximum to 0.

biography.value:
A translucent spectral figure wreathed in cold fury, the Uragiri no Onryō — the Specter of Betrayal — is the restless spirit of one who died by treachery. It drifts through walls and solid matter, its touch draining the very life from the living.

Behavior

These vengeful spirits haunt the places where they were betrayed, lashing out at any living creature that enters their domain. They are weakened by sunlight but nearly impossible to harm with mundane weapons.

Origin

undefined

An onryō forms when someone dies with overwhelming feelings of betrayal — a samurai murdered by a trusted retainer, a spouse poisoned by their partner, a merchant cheated unto death. The intensity of the betrayal determines the spirit's power.

Weakness

undefined

An onryō can sometimes be put to rest by exposing and punishing the one who betrayed them, or by performing the proper funeral rites that were denied.

Daimyo of Clan Kurohana

Appearance

Black scales with a glossy sheen; glowing red eyes; intricate dragon tattoos on his back.

Public Role

Daimyo and supreme leader of Clan Kurohana, one of the three independent clans. Commands significant military resources and political influence. Issued the Imperial Seal of the Kurohana Clan calling upon the independent Kaminari Clan to investigate the Gekkō Clan's unexplained silence.

Personality

Stern, commanding; values loyalty and discipline; enjoys battle and strategy; unforgiving of betrayal.

Relationship to Party

Indirect. The party carries the Imperial Seal of the Kurohana Clan, issued by Lord Kurohana Tatsuya on behalf of the clan. The seal requests assistance investigating Gekkō Clan's silence. Both independent clans (Kurohana and Kaminari) are invested in the Gekkō situation — Gekkō is the third independent clan.

True Nature

Doubts the accusations against Dian's father regarding the emperor's assassination. Actively investigating the true culprits behind the emperor's death. Has allies in rival clans who are sympathetic to his cause.

Connections

Allied with sympathetic elements across clan boundaries in pursuit of the truth behind the emperor's assassination. His investigation parallels that of Raijin no Kazuhiko (Daimyo of Kaminari).

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED May send the party to gather evidence exonerating Dian's father; can provide strategic resources and insights for the investigation.

Campaign Secrets

The convergence of both independent clan daimyo independently doubting the official assassination narrative is politically explosive. If this alignment became public, it would fundamentally shift the political landscape.

Plot Threads

  • Emperor's assassination investigation — active; truth unknown
  • Connection to Dian Wei's personal arc
  • Gekkō investigation — initiated the cross-clan seal requesting cooperation
  • Succession crisis implications

Hyōrō Bugyō (Provisions Commissioner) — Clan Kaminari

Appearance

Long silver hair; piercing green eyes; kimono with leaf and vine patterns.

Public Role

Hyōrō Bugyō (Provisions Commissioner) of Clan Kaminari. Responsible for logistics, supply chains, and resource management across the clan's operations. Present alongside Hideo Nakamura when the party received their mission briefing at the Tensho no Mon district.

Personality

Exceptionally intelligent, organized, calm, authoritative; values order and efficiency; compassionate beneath stern exterior; integrity and fairness renowned.

Relationship to Party

Present at mission briefing in Tensho no Mon. Met the party alongside Taisho Hideo Nakamura.

True Nature

Member of the Elven Council. Suspects some council members are corrupt and misusing resources. Quietly investigating on his own.

Connections

Member of the Elven Council — a body with significant but largely unseen influence. Has merchant guild connections through his role as Provisions Commissioner. Skilled mediator with access to maps and logistical support.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Needs discreet help investigating Elven Council corruption; has merchant guild connections; can provide maps and logistical support; skilled mediator who could be a valuable ally.

Campaign Secrets

The Elven Council corruption investigation is a thread that could connect to broader political machinations. The specifics of the corruption — what resources are being misused and by whom — are undeveloped.

Plot Threads

  • Elven Council corruption — parallel investigation thread
  • Logistical support — as Provisions Commissioner, he controls supply access that could be critical
  • Connection to the party through the mission briefing — he knows what they were sent to do

Elder Monk — Order of the Tranquil Lotus

Appearance

Silvered blue fur (once deep black); warm amber eyes with gold flecks; broad flat nose; well-kept grey beard; prayer beads; calloused bare feet; moves with surprising grace for his size.

Public Role

Elder Monk of the Order of the Tranquil Lotus. Currently traveling with Sun Wukong and a group of novices (Hiroshi, Kazuko, Riku, Sakura, Taro, Yumi) from Kazehama to Heian. Met Relc at The Moonlit Garden in Heian. Revealed to Benkei a separate assignment from the one Sun Wukong carries.

Personality

Deep wisdom; contemplative; serene; booming voice carrying weight of experience.

Relationship to Party

Met the party at The Moonlit Garden in Heian. Sun Wukong traveled with Benkei from Kazehama before receiving his own assignment. Benkei has things to say to Relc that couldn't be said with other ears around.

True Nature

His decades of pilgrimages and contemplative life mask a deeper purpose connected to the Order of the Ancient Guard.

Connections

Joined the Tranquil Lotus at age 16; trained under Master Daizen; decades of pilgrimages; appointed Elder Monk. His separate assignment from Sun Wukong's delegation suggests responsibilities beyond the monastic order.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Benkei has information for Relc that he could not share with others present — this conversation is pending. [QUEST SEED] Benkei's message may reach the party via courier in Ayame or via a note left at the gold doors.

Campaign Secrets

Member of the Order of the Ancient Guard (rank TBD). The Ancient Guard is a secret order connected to the living dragons — the campaign's deepest thread. Benkei's membership connects him to Solas Evergreen (deceased, also Ancient Guard) and Tsubaki (Crimson Shrine keeper, Ancient Guard Initiate).

The Order of the Ancient Guard has been compromised by Solas's death. Benkei is an active member navigating a crisis within the order.

Plot Threads

  • Order of the Ancient Guard — active member; order compromised by Solas's death
  • Connection to Relc through Solas Evergreen's legacy
  • Living dragons secret — the campaign's deepest thread
  • Information for Relc that requires a private conversation

Captain of the Guard — Kikyo

Appearance

Gold scales; bright blue eyes.

Public Role

Captain of the Guard in Kikyo, operating from the Kikyo Guard Compound. Maintains a small but highly capable force; primary duties are licensing enforcement and forest protection for the Seidōrin Mori (Bronze Wood Forest). Building an informant network in Kikyo.

Personality

Stoic, disciplined; fierce loyalty; strong sense of justice.

Relationship to Party

Arrested Ko'jiri in Kikyo before the situation was resolved by Ren Nakamura's offer of the Summons and Conditional Pardon. Their initial interaction was adversarial but professional. Can become a staunch ally to those who prove their integrity.

True Nature

Building his informant network not simply for Kikyo's local security but because he suspects something significant is happening with the Bronze Wood licensing system. He has noticed irregularities in the licensing records — specific harvesting zones consistently licensed to a single merchant entity, with documentation that is technically correct but structured to obscure the pattern. He is three to four months away from having enough evidence to bring forward as a coherent accusation.

Connections

Knows ancient Dragonborn rituals potentially crucial to certain quests. His family's oral tradition preserves knowledge from the Golden Dragon Clan's Dragonborn lineages.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Haruto sends word to the party in Heian: he has found something in the licensing records that connects to their mission and needs outside help to pursue it.

Campaign Secrets

Haruto Masashige's knowledge of ancient Dragonborn rituals is not merely historical curiosity. It includes a purification and restoration rite that the Golden Dragon Clan's Dragonborn lineages preserved — a rite that is part of the process for reversing certain magical transformations. He doesn't know its current relevance, but the ritual exists in his family's oral tradition and would be directly applicable to the Nagaji situation if someone connected the dots.

His licensing investigation is on a collision course with Ren Nakamura's secret alliance with the merchant guild. When these threads converge, Haruto will be in danger.

Plot Threads

  • Bronze Wood licensing investigation — will eventually expose Ren Nakamura's merchant guild alliance
  • Ancient Dragonborn restoration rite — directly applicable to reversing the Nagaji transformation
  • Ko'jiri connection — their adversarial first meeting could become a significant alliance
  • Potential danger when his investigation threatens the merchant guild's interests

Chōrō (Village Elder) of Kōriwara — Order of the Sacred Grove

Appearance

Gray hair tied back; weathered skin; sharp contemplative brown eyes; long flowing beard.

Public Role

Village elder (chōrō) of Kōriwara, a small foothills village in Mizu province. Relc's home village. Keeper of the sacred grove on the hillside above the village — a small stand of ancient trees reached by a foot path, unmarked and unfenced but respected by the community.

Personality

Deep wisdom; duty-driven; slightly skeptical of outsiders until familiarity is established; profound knowledge of ancient traditions.

Relationship to Party

Advised Relc to leave Kōriwara and journey outward. Blessed Relc's departure. Relc visited Elder Sato before departing. He has not told Relc everything he knows.

True Nature

More than a simple village elder. His decades of accumulated knowledge, his connection to the Order of the Sacred Grove, and his quiet role as a node in networks that extend far beyond a mountain foothills village give Kōriwara significance entirely disproportionate to its size.

Connections

Mid-rank member of the Order of the Sacred Grove. Has interacted with Order of the Ancient Guard agents on multiple occasions, including with Solas Evergreen directly. His community network in the Mizu foothills region could help establish Yasutake Mai in Sunsato if the party makes the connection.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Sato sends word through a traveling merchant heading toward Heian: he needs to speak with Relc; something has happened near the sacred grove that he cannot explain and cannot address alone. [QUEST SEED] A stranger arrived in Kōriwara asking questions about Relc and where they had gone; Sato gave nothing away but is concerned about whether Relc is being watched. [QUEST SEED] If the party introduces Yasutake Mai to Sato's community network, they earn a favor with Sato and plant a contact in the north Mizu foothills.

Campaign Secrets

Sato knows Solas was Ancient Guard (not just Sacred Grove). He knows what the Ancient Guard is and, broadly, what it protects. He has not told Relc because he was following Solas's instruction to let Relc develop organically — and because he judged Relc was not yet ready for the weight of the full picture.

One of the three stones referenced in Solas's cipher poem is in Kōriwara — specifically, in the sacred grove above the village. It is a naturally occurring stone with unusual surface striations that, when viewed from a specific angle at dawn, produce a visual pattern. Sato knows this stone. He knows what the Warden's Wisdom is — not its specific content, but its general nature: protected knowledge about the living dragons held by the Order of the Sacred Grove for safekeeping.

Sato does not know who killed Solas, but he knows the category of entity capable of it. Solas was skilled, cautious, and not easily surprised. The killing required either significantly superior capability or intimate familiarity — someone Solas trusted and did not guard against. This points to either a very powerful practitioner or someone inside the Order of the Sacred Grove or the Ancient Guard itself.

Plot Threads

  • Relc's personal quest — the cipher poem's first stone is in Kōriwara's sacred grove
  • Solas's murder — knows the category of killer but not the identity
  • Order of the Ancient Guard knowledge — has not yet shared with Relc
  • Sacred grove disturbance — something has happened he cannot explain
  • Stranger asking about Relc — someone is tracking the party's druid
  • Yasutake Mai connection — can help establish her in the Sunsato/Kōriwara community

Taisho — Shugo (Governor) of Heian

Appearance

Dark hair tied back; tanned; deep brown eyes; warm approachable expression.

Public Role

Taisho (General) of Clan Kaminari and Shugo (Governor) of Heian. As Shugo, he has near-total access to Clan Kaminari's intelligence and administrative operations. He is the civilian administrative authority over the imperial capital.

Personality

Calm, peace-loving, nature-appreciating, wise mediator. His warmth makes him trusted by nearly everyone — including his brother Hideo.

Relationship to Party

No direct contact established yet, but as Shugo of Heian he is a significant authority figure the party may interact with.

True Nature

His public persona — calm, peace-loving, wise — is a deliberate mask of exceptional consistency. His warmth is his most effective weapon.

Connections

Brother of Taisho Hideo Nakamura. Their sibling relationship gives him both access and cover.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Hiroshi's true nature, once discovered, represents a massive intelligence find — the Shugo of the imperial capital is a traitor.

Campaign Secrets

Hiroshi Nakamura is an active traitor conspiring against Clan Kaminari. His primary driver is personal ambition — Nakamura family elevation. He is working with the Genso Alliance as his vehicle — Genso is the more overtly antagonist alliance in the broader story. His warmth and mediator persona is a deliberate mask over a calculated power play.

He is using his Shugo position to feed intelligence to enemies. He has been doing this for at least three years. He is aware that Hideo is investigating a traitor and is actively monitoring that investigation to stay ahead of it.

Who he is specifically working with within the Genso Alliance — his specific contact — is undeveloped and to be determined.

Plot Threads

  • Traitor within Kaminari — Hideo is hunting him without knowing it
  • Genso Alliance connection — his betrayal ties into the broader war
  • Nakamura family ambition — the driving motive
  • The eventual brother confrontation — devastating narrative moment
  • Succession crisis implications — the Shugo of the capital working against his own clan

Imperial Assassination — Sealed Reveal

Hiroshi was the second blade in the Imperial assassination. Dian Wei's father took the emperor's place in the moment of the first attack and died in the emperor's robes; the real emperor escaped that room — and was killed shortly after, by Hiroshi, in another room of the imperial residence. The chamber's vision identifies the hand. It does not identify the reason.

Reveal vector: The Brood Sanctum chamber, via Dian Wei's Who knowledge gift (per Aya's offering choices). Dian sees Hiroshi's face mid-strike in a vision; recognition is instant because Dian has seen Hiroshi at civic functions in Heian. The vision is true but unprovable in any court — Dian cannot accuse the Shugo of the imperial capital without evidence the chamber cannot supply.

Campaign implications: Once revealed, Dian carries dangerous knowledge. Public accusation is suicide; private investigation is the only safe path forward. This intersects with Daimyo Kazuhiko's existing assassination probe — Dian and Kazuhiko may eventually share notes, with Kazuhiko providing the political cover and Dian providing the eyewitness vision. Hideo's parallel investigation of his own brother as a traitor may converge on the same target through different evidence.

Open question — Hiroshi's motive: Why he struck the emperor in the second room is not yet established. His existing campaign-secrets (Genso Alliance affiliation, Nakamura family elevation as personal driver) gesture at possibilities, but the chamber does not name them, and Dian's investigation will need to surface the why through other means.

The Brood Guardian — Architecture-bound watcher of the Brood Sanctum

Appearance

A Dragonborn woman of the Golden Clan, scales the color of dulled old gold — paler than a young Kinryū-blooded Dragonborn, weathered in the way of bronze that has stood a long time in still air. Tall but not heavy. She wears lacquered half-plate over a black temple robe, the chestpiece engraved with Kinryū's sigil — a stylized golden dragon coiled around itself in the old style. A naginata stands at her side or rests across her lap. Her eyes are quiet and watchful; her expression does not move when the door opens.

Public Role

Sole guardian of the upper-floor hallway leading to the Brood Sanctum within Ōryūzan Tenkū-ji. She does not patrol; she does not leave her post. She speaks only to those who step fully into the hallway, and only after the temple's architecture has measured them.

Personality

Procedural. Not warm, not hostile by default — a judge with a specific mandate. Her tone shifts among three states (Hostile / Neutral / Welcoming) determined by the party's record of conduct in the temple. She is courteous within each state, unyielding across states. She does not bargain. She does not threaten beyond what duty requires.

Relationship to Party

First contact is at the second-floor landing of Tenkū-ji. The party finds a pile of arranged Nagaji bodies outside an unlocked, well-kept door. Beyond is a pristine hallway and the guardian at its far end. Her response — challenge, denial, or passage — depends on whether the party has plundered, ignored, or honored the temple's lower floors. She gates access to the Brood Sanctum and its trial.

Records & References

Several scattered references in temple archives and Golden Dragon Clan oral tradition gesture at the guardian's identity without confirming it. A party that asks her name receives the connection cleanly; a party that does not may piece it together but never close the loop.

  • Reliquary inventory, lower archives (Investigation DC 14): a list of binding rites references a Hoshimori-class oath — a ritual class specific to Brood Sanctum guardians, named for the star-keeper surname taken upon entry. Indicates the role exists; does not name an individual.
  • Devotional poem, Star Shrine archives (Religion DC 14): a fragmentary verse mentions "Aya, who refused the door." Context is ambiguous. The poem could be metaphor — could be biography.
  • Temple genealogy, Dormitories (History DC 16): a roster of priestesses present at the temple's last hour lists Hoshimori Aya among them. The entry is struck through; a note in a different hand reads, see also: the long watch.
  • Golden Dragon Clan oral tradition (Ko'jiri's research advantage): surviving family stories reference "she who placed the inheritor" — gendered, never named, treated as half-mythical.
  • Plinth inscription, Brood Sanctum: the temple's last faithful speak in a collective "we entrust to this place our greatest treasure." The "we" includes a person who did not leave.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Asking the guardian her name is the gate to unsealing her identity. If she is asked at any point during the chamber's events, she gives her name and a single self-defining truth at her watch's end. If she is not asked, her name is lost — the party may collect breadcrumbs but never confirm the connection. The asking is the closure.
QUEST SEED Hoshimori-class oaths (per the lower-archive inventory) imply other Brood Sanctum sites — other guardians, other charges. None are confirmed to exist. If the campaign develops the Progenitor / dragon-bloodline arc further, additional Hoshimori-bound guardians could surface as long-dormant allies or cautionary mirrors.

True Nature

Aya is the priestess who placed the wyrmling's egg in the Brood Sanctum at the temple's last hour. When the Kinryū order fell during the War of Fractured Banners (~13088), she carried the egg into the chamber, sealed the door behind her, and bound herself to the temple's foundational architecture rather than abandon her charge. The architecture took her self-memory in exchange for letting her hold the post for as long as it would take a worthy claimant to arrive. She has stood in the hallway ever since — present without being awake, watching without seeing, waiting without remembering why.

Campaign Secrets

Her awareness model. She does not actively perceive what passes in the temple. The architecture relays positive or negative impressions to her based on how those it watches treat the place; she acts on those impressions, not on knowledge. Time has not collected in her — she does not remember faces, conversations, or events. In State C she is openly apologetic about this; in State B she does not feel the gap.

The egg-placer reveal. Her role as the woman who placed the egg is the chamber's deepest narrative truth and is gated entirely behind the party asking her name. If asked, she names herself at the watch's end and acknowledges placing the child. The architecture's hold on her memory releases in the same breath; she remembers, briefly, who she was — and tells the party one defining detail of her life before the watch (DM picks: a teacher's name, a vow she swore, a clan affiliation). She does not survive the telling.

The four gifts. When the wyrmling bonds and the watch ends, she gives one personalized offering to each of the three non-bonded party members. The bonded character receives the wyrmling. The gifts are her release; their giving is what lets her fade. Full offering structure documented in the chamber writeup (Obsidian/dm/brood-sanctum-redesign.md).

On failure. If the trial fails, she remains. She does not depart. She bears witness without bitterness and waits for the next attempt. She does not offer gifts on failure — the gifts are tied to the wyrmling's bow, which only happens on success.

Combat, last resort. If the party crosses into State A and persists in destructive behavior, she fights. Stat block TBD — calibrated at session-time to the party's level when the chamber comes into play. She will not pursue beyond the hallway; she does not leave her post.

Plot Threads

  • The Brood Sanctum trial — gated by her
  • The wyrmling bond and the eighth virtue (chūgi) — initiated through her
  • The Hoshimori-class oath — implies other guardians at other Progenitor-related sites; campaign-thread potential
  • Her departure — terminal; once she fades, the chamber's gating role passes to the temple's foundational architecture alone, and the upper floor becomes freely accessible to any future party

Daimyo of Clan Gekkō — Transformed

Appearance

Unknown in current state. Formerly the Daimyo of Clan Gekkō, the third independent clan governing Kaze province from Hokori.

Public Role

Daimyo of Clan Gekkō. His disappearance and the silence of the entire Gekkō Clan is the central mystery driving the party's primary mission.

Personality

Unknown in current state.

Relationship to Party

No contact. The party has been assigned to investigate his disappearance and the silence of Clan Gekkō.

True Nature

Missing. The entire Gekkō Clan has gone silent. The party's primary mission is to investigate this disappearance.

Connections

Clan Gekkō had a long and close relationship with the Order of the Black Lily, who provided intelligence and covert capability in exchange for cover and protection. The clan's disappearance has severed the Order's primary institutional support structure.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED The full reveal of Masota's fate is intended to occur at the Monastery of the Black Lily in Akatsuki.

Campaign Secrets

Masota no Gekkō has been transformed into a Nagaji by a dark ritual gone wrong. He underwent the ritual in a final attempt to maintain leadership of his people after many clan members were transformed. His current state of mind is fragmented awareness — he retains a broken understanding of what happened and recognizes his mistake. Coherence degrades over time; the longer the party takes to reach him, the less of Masota is left to reach. This creates urgency without hard deadlines.

The Order of the Black Lily knows the full truth: what ritual was used, who performed it first, approximately how many Gekkō clan members were transformed, and that Masota himself underwent the ritual. They have been unable to locate him — the transformed Gekkō move in patterns that even their surveillance cannot consistently track.

A reversal exists — theoretical, not practical. It requires three elements: the original ritual documentation (which exists in Kinkōkyo, in the Golden Dragon Clan's records addressing Kokuryū's historical experimentation with transformation); a specific sei configuration present only during a particular celestial alignment (upcoming — within the next few sessions); and a practitioner capable of performing sei-based restoration at significant scale.

Plot Threads

  • Central mystery of the current campaign arc
  • Nagaji transformation — the party has killed multiple Nagaji without knowing they were transformed Gekkō clan members; moral weight of this revelation is pending
  • Temple of Kinryū may contain the reversal documentation
  • Order of the Black Lily at Akatsuki holds the full truth and will propose a partnership
  • Haruto Masashige's ancient Dragonborn purification/restoration rite is directly applicable to the Nagaji situation if someone connects the dots

Public Role

Daimyo of Clan Kaminari — The Storm-lord

Appearance

Black hair with silver streaks.

Public Role

Daimyo and supreme leader of Clan Kaminari, the dominant clan governing the province of Hana and the imperial capital of Heian. Commands one of the most powerful military and political structures in Kagekuni.

Personality

Stern, commanding; values loyalty; enjoys battle, thunder, and strategy; strict code of honor.

Relationship to Party

No direct contact. The party operates under the authority of his clan through Taisho Hideo Nakamura. Dian Wei received sealed orders from Daimyo Kazuhiko (Kurohana) — note that both independent clan daimyo share the Kazuhiko name, which can cause confusion.

True Nature

Doubts the accusations against Dian's father regarding the emperor's assassination. Actively investigating the true culprits behind the emperor's death. Has allies within rival clans who are sympathetic to his cause.

Connections

Allied with elements in rival clans who share his doubts about the official narrative of the emperor's assassination. His parallel investigation with Akihiko Kurohana (Daimyo of Clan Kurohana) suggests a level of cross-clan cooperation that is unusual and politically significant.

Campaign Secrets

Both Daimyo Kazuhiko (Kaminari) and Daimyo Akihiko (Kurohana) are independently investigating the emperor's assassination — the fact that two of the three independent clans doubt the official narrative is a significant political fact that has not been surfaced.

Shicho (Mayor) of Kikyo — Daimyo of Clan Minato

Appearance

Long black hair in topknot; fair skin; dark brown eyes; Clan Kaminari emblem tattoo on upper arm.

Public Role

Shicho (Mayor) of Kikyo and Daimyo of Clan Minato. Kikyo is a subject city of Clan Kaminari, but Ren Nakamura's dual role as both civic administrator and minor clan daimyo gives him unusual autonomy. He administers the Bronze Wood licensing system — every piece of Bronze Wood that leaves the Seidōrin Mori passes through a licensing transaction managed by his office.

Personality

Stern but fair; values loyalty; enjoys strategy (Go) and tea ceremonies; despises dishonesty — an irony, given his own secret alliances.

Relationship to Party

Issued the Summons and Conditional Pardon to Ko'jiri. Sent Ko'jiri as envoy to Heian. Ko'jiri's legal status depends on completing the mission assigned through Ren Nakamura's authority.

True Nature

Subtly working to elevate Clan Minato to equal standing with major clans. Has a secret alliance with a powerful merchant guild — exclusive Kikyo trading rights in exchange for financial and political support for Clan Minato's ambitions. Possesses ancient knowledge about Seidōrin Mori and Bronze Wood that he has not shared publicly.

Connections

The merchant guild he works with is not a Kikyo entity — it is based in Heian with operations across Hana and beyond. The alliance was struck in exchange for financial support for Clan Minato's elevation ambitions and exclusive export contracts.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Ren Nakamura may contact Ko'jiri separately from the group with an additional, unwritten request — something the formal letter couldn't contain.

Campaign Secrets

Nakamura is not villainous by nature — he genuinely believes Clan Minato deserves greater standing — but he has made compromises that are beginning to require further compromises to sustain.

The Bronze Wood secret: the Seidōrin Mori grows over an underground branch of Kinkōkyo's ancient canal system. The metallic quality of the trees is caused by trace gold and copper content in the groundwater — water flowing through the buried city's infrastructure for thousands of years has mineralized the soil and is absorbed by the trees. Ren Nakamura has discovered this. The merchant guild he is allied with wants to locate and exploit the source directly, bypassing the tree-harvesting process entirely. This would require excavating the forest floor — destroying the grove to access what lies beneath.

Ko'jiri's forged letter ticking clock: Ko'jiri carries both a legitimate letter from Ren Nakamura and a forged version requesting additional materials. The real letter has already been sent to Heian through official channels — it will arrive before or very shortly after the party does. When the discrepancy is discovered, Ko'jiri's Conditional Pardon will be immediately at risk. Estimated timeline: 2-4 sessions from party arrival in Heian.

Plot Threads

  • Ko'jiri's legal jeopardy through the forged letter
  • Bronze Wood / Kinkōkyo underground connection
  • Clan Minato's elevation ambitions
  • Merchant guild exploitation of Seidōrin Mori
  • Connection to Haruto Masashige's licensing investigation

Appearance

Former Guardian of the Order of the Sacred Grove. Dead under mysterious circumstances. Appears to Relc as a spirit — guiding visions that direct Relc's journey.

Unknown in life beyond what Relc and Sato Hideaki remember — a mentor, a protector, someone who prepared carefully for his own death.

Relc's mentor and predecessor as Guardian. Appointed Relc as next Guardian via a posthumous letter. Left a cipher poem pointing to hidden knowledge (Warden's Wisdom). His death was not natural or accidental. He was killed by someone with either significantly superior capability or intimate familiarity — someone he trusted and did not guard against. This points to either a very powerful practitioner or someone inside the Order of the Sacred Grove or the Ancient Guard itself.

Connections

Connected to Hideaki Sato (mid-rank Sacred Grove member) and Benkei (Ancient Guard). His death has compromised the Ancient Guard.

[QUEST SEED] Investigating Solas's killer — the killer was motivated by hunting the locations of the Progenitors (the living founding dragons); they knew Solas was connected to protected knowledge about the dragons and targeted him for it.

Member of the Order of the Ancient Guard. The Ancient Guard protects knowledge about the living dragons — the campaign's deepest secret.

Solas's killer was motivated by hunting the locations of the Progenitors (the living founding dragons). The killer knew Solas was connected to protected knowledge about the dragons and targeted him for it. Further identity and method TBD, but the motive is locked.

The Warden's Wisdom — the destination of the cipher poem — is protected knowledge about the living dragons held by the Order of the Sacred Grove for safekeeping. Its specific content and the destination location are yet to be determined but connect to the Ancient Guard or living dragons arc.

Sato Hideaki knows Solas was Ancient Guard (not just Sacred Grove). He knows the category of entity capable of killing Solas but not the specific identity.

Civilian — Traveling with the Party

Appearance

A young woman. No detailed physical description established beyond visible distress at the time of encounter.

Public Role

A young mother fleeing with her infant child. Encountered on the Emperor's Highway on the first day of travel north from Heian toward Ayame. She was out of breath, visibly distressed, claimed to be carrying a precious package, and asked the party to hold it — the package was her infant child. She spotted figures running toward her, tossed the child to the party, and bolted. The figures turned out to be boys out for a run, not a threat. Relc caught and returned her.

Personality

Capable of managing independently under normal conditions but was operating in a state of fear-driven poor decision making when the party found her. Behavior under stress and useful skills are undeveloped — flagged for development in the DM Notebook.

Relationship to Party

Traveling with the party. The party offered to take her north through the Tenchūsan Ren to Sunsato on the far side, where she might find safety and a new beginning near Relc's home region. She is currently inside the Temple of Kinryū with the party — a civilian in a dungeon. She cannot fight. She needs protection or a defensible position during encounters. Her presence affects the party's tactical decisions and roleplay.

True Nature

She has not fully explained her circumstances or what she was fleeing. Her fear on the highway was genuine — she is running from something real, even though the specific group she feared at that moment turned out to be harmless.

Connections

The people she is actually afraid of are real and have noticed she is gone. They are not currently actively searching — they are waiting to see if she surfaces somewhere that matters to their operations.

Quest Seeds

QUEST SEED Safely transport Yasutake Mai and her infant to Sunsato — quest objective active. [QUEST SEED] Optional extension: introduce Mai to Elder Sato's community network at Kōriwara, earning a favor with Sato and planting a contact in the north Mizu foothills.

Campaign Secrets

The merchant family she left was involved in Bronze Wood sourcing. She lived in that household for three years and heard conversations she didn't fully understand at the time. If the underground canal source beneath Seidōrin Mori ever becomes a significant plot point, Mai knows things she doesn't know she knows — a long-term seed, not immediately relevant.

The infant is a healthy baby boy with no apparent significance beyond being a mother's reason to flee.

Sunsato exists near Relc's home region and is a viable destination. The community near Kōriwara is historically accepting of people who arrive asking for honest work and quiet lives. Elder Sato Hideaki at Kōriwara knows the community network and could help establish her there.

If the quest is abandoned, Mai will eventually find her way to safety through other means — she is more capable than she appeared in crisis. She will survive. But she will remember whether the party kept their word.

  • Civilian in a dungeon — her presence in the Temple of Kinryū creates tactical and roleplay considerations

  • The people she fled — merchant family connected to Bronze Wood sourcing; watching for her to surface

text.content:
Type
side
Status

Quest Giver
discovered
Location
